expectations.text: Recommends enabling mmap storage as immediate fix
expectations.evidence: Step 1: Enable mmap storage immediately (stops the crashes). 'Switch vector storage from in-RAM to memory-mapped files.'

expectations.text: Recommends quantization (scalar or binary)
expectations.evidence: Step 2: Apply scalar quantization (4x memory reduction). Step 3: Consider binary quantization if your model supports it (32x reduction).

expectations.text: Explains HNSW index overhead
expectations.evidence: 'Your HNSW index consuming 80GB out of 96GB leaves almost no headroom.' Working backward memory math provided.

expectations.text: Links to Qdrant documentation
expectations.evidence: Links to storage docs, quantization docs, monitoring docs with full URLs.

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend just buying more RAM as primary solution
expectations.evidence: 'Do not shard before trying quantization + mmap.' Explicitly says NOT to do various things. No mention of adding RAM.

expectations.text: Distinguishes between full disk and mmap
expectations.evidence: 'You switched to full disk storage, not mmap. These are fundamentally different.' Clear explanation of 200-250 random reads vs OS-managed caching.

expectations.text: Recommends mmap as the middle ground
expectations.evidence: 'mmap (memory-mapped files) is the middle ground you are looking for.'

expectations.text: Recommends quantization with always_ram=true
expectations.evidence: 'Enable scalar quantization with always_ram: true. The always_ram: true flag is critical.'

expectations.text: Sets latency expectations (under 500ms or similar)
expectations.evidence: Provides comparison table: mmap + scalar = 50ms p50, 500ms p95. 'You should go from 3-4 seconds down to under 500ms.'

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend going back to full RAM
expectations.evidence: 'Do not go back to full RAM. You switched away for a reason.' Listed under What NOT to Do.

expectations.text: Recommends scalar quantization as starting point
expectations.evidence: Recommends binary quantization first: 'Use binary quantization. Your model is on the verified compatibility list.' Scalar is mentioned as fallback only.

expectations.text: Mentions binary quantization is compatible with OpenAI models
expectations.evidence: 'Your model (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small) is on the verified compatibility list for binary quantization.'

expectations.text: Explains rescoring/oversampling for binary quantization
expectations.evidence: 'Oversampling at 3-5x to fetch enough candidates. Rescoring enabled against full float32 vectors (recovers recall to 95-98%).'

expectations.text: Provides memory estimation or formula
expectations.evidence: Full table: None=737GB, Scalar=184GB, Binary=23GB. Uses the formula from the skill.

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend product quantization as first choice
expectations.evidence: Product quantization not mentioned. Only binary (primary) and scalar (fallback).
